corpus_intended_use: Preregistered public development corpus for the Codex-only three-arm comparison. Its cases are built so that the deciding rule often lives in the full reviewer workflow references rather than in the pattern catalog alone. It is not sealed and does not establish generalization.
corpus_contamination_risk: The corpus is inspectable and was written by the same author who wrote the reviewer references it exercises. Every result must disclose that exposure and remain development evidence.

scoring.source_rendering_contract: Each embedded source line is prefixed with its 1-based number, right-aligned to six columns, and a tab, as `nl -ba` prints it. The prefix is display-only; findings must cite that number as `line`.
scoring.label_semantics_contract: Findings still match exact (pattern_id, severity, file, line) tuples. A finding label matches when a report hits its primary tuple or any accepted_alternatives tuple, and counts as one true positive however many of those tuples are reported. An optional label is excluded from true-positive and false-negative denominators; a report matching it is not a false positive and is counted separately as an optional match. fp_guard labels keep their meaning.
scoring.stability_contract: A finding or optional label is stable when the number of successful repetitions that matched any of its tuples meets the strict-majority rule. A stable prediction is a false positive only when it matches no finding or optional label tuple.

schedule.freeze_policy: Freeze sources, labels, and protocol before the first measured run. Any later edit creates a new version.
schedule.design_disclosure: Reviewer holdout v16 asks whether the three reviewer contract fixes of commit 9e73a6c (the semantic-review.md #20 row aligned to the pattern-reference.md evidence rule, a #23 primary line in pattern-reference.md, and P1 severity for a #2 partial verification) help on a corpus they were not derived from. The fixes were derived from v10 outcomes, so v16 reuses the frozen v9 corpus unchanged by path and digest (30 cases, 16 Playwright, 14 Cypress) on the single Codex host gpt-6-sol at the codex-cli 0.155.1 floor. It runs the full and catalog-only arms under two preregistered skill revisions pinned by skill digest: before is the skill at 769f1f6, byte-identical to the skill at c21d4f0, and after is the skill at 9e73a6c, which also carries 92f5bdf. 92f5bdf moves the scanner command lines from SKILL.md into references/scanner-workflow.md; both files are in the full-arm prompt, so the full-arm prompt bytes differ by that move as well as by the three fixes, although a tool-less holdout call cannot run the scanner. The catalog-only prompt differs only by the two pattern-reference.md additions (#2 severity and #23 primary line); the #20 fix is not in it. No no-skill arm is run because its prompt embeds no skill file and is byte-identical under both revisions. The decision is a paired stratified case bootstrap of after minus before, preregistered in revision_comparison, not the three-arm skill-lift comparison. V16 carries v11's infrastructure-retry policy unchanged, v13's usage capture, and v15's enforced output schema, which Codex receives with --output-schema; the schema's pattern_id enum covers every v9 label and accepted alternative. It keeps v12's per-report thresholds, seed, strict-majority stability rule, numbered sources, scoring contract, and five repetitions. The v9 corpus was built by the same author who wrote the fixes, it already ran on Codex gpt-5.6-sol under v9 with public reports, and the skill was revised after those results, so both revisions may already fit it; only the difference between them is tested. Those runs do not train models. The corpus is public development evidence, not sealed, and does not establish generalization; one host supports no cross-provider claim.

execution_identity.run_identity_capture: Capture the resolved runner path and CLI version in each report. Do not pin user-specific absolute paths or binary digests in this public protocol.
execution_identity.attestation_limit: Reported execution identity is provenance, not cryptographic attestation.

infrastructure_retry.contract: A scheduled call whose attempt times out, exits non-zero with a CLI usage, weekly, or rate limit message, or exits zero with output that is not one strict JSON payload is re-invoked in a freshly prepared identical workspace at the same schedule position, up to max_attempts_per_call attempts. Every attempt is recorded with its number, reason, and exit code. The final attempt is the one scored; an unscoreable final attempt stays an infrastructure error. A scoreable output is never retried, whatever its findings.

output_schema.contract: The runner passes the schema, serialized as compact sorted-key JSON whose sha256 is schema_sha256, to the host CLI's native structured-output option: Claude Code with --output-format json and --json-schema, Codex with --output-schema. The model answer is Claude's structured_output object, serialized as compact JSON, or Codex's final agent message. That answer then goes through the unchanged strict single-JSON-payload parser and findings validator. No fence or other output normalization is applied. A Claude result without an object structured_output, or an answer the strict parser refuses, is malformed output under the infrastructure-retry policy. The pattern_id enum is the output-legend vocabulary shown to every arm, the prompt is unchanged, and the schema applies identically to every arm.

prompt_arms.matrix_requirement: Run full and catalog-only once for each preregistered skill revision. No no-skill arm is run: its prompt embeds no skill file, so it is byte-identical under both revisions.

revision_comparison.question: Do the three reviewer contract fixes of commit 9e73a6c (the #20 row of semantic-review.md aligned to the pattern-reference.md evidence rule, a #23 primary line in pattern-reference.md, and P1 severity for a #2 partial verification) raise stable F1 on the v9 corpus, which they were not derived from?
revision_comparison.skill_binding: A run refuses to start unless the evaluated skill directory's skill_sha256 equals one revision's pinned skill_sha256, and each report records that digest. skill_tree is the git tree of skills/e2e-reviewer at source_commit; git archive of source_commit reproduces the directory. The comparison binds each report to the revision whose digest it records and recomputes its prompt digest from that revision's files.

uncertainty.interpretation_limit: Bootstrap intervals describe case-resampling sensitivity on this fixed public case set. They do not quantify model-run stochasticity and are not population confidence intervals, independent replications, or release-grade causal inference.

decision.semantics: SUPPORTED when, in the full arm, the after-minus-before stable F1 point estimate is at least 0, its paired-bootstrap 95% lower bound is at least 0, and the after revision's stable guard-hit rate is not higher than the before revision's. NOT_SUPPORTED when all four reports are valid and complete and any of those conditions fails. INCONCLUSIVE when any report is missing, invalid, not execution complete, or has an unscored run, or when the reports break the execution order or the elapsed-time limit. The catalog-only after-minus-before deltas are reported descriptively and do not enter the decision.

claim_policy.supported: The fixes did not lower full-arm stable F1 or raise the stable guard-hit rate on this fixed public corpus, host, CLI floor, schedule, and output schema. A zero lower bound is a non-inferiority reading; only a positive lower bound shows an improvement.
claim_policy.not_supported: No claim that the fixes help on a corpus they were not derived from.

decision.point_estimate_limits: Threshold crossings on this small fixed public development corpus are descriptive signals. The corpus is public and inspectable. Confidence intervals accompany point estimates; sealing, independent blind evaluation after publication, cryptographic runner attestation, cross-provider replication, and population-level generalization are not established.

cross_host_decision.aggregation_intent: Codex-only protocol; the single declared host is evaluated directly and no cross-provider claim is allowed.

evidence_limitations.message: prompt-complete zero-tool execution stages parent authentication material, not a disposable scoped credential; this report is development evidence and is not release-eligible
